_comment: Connector-specific edits a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present (and every banned anti-pattern still absent) and fails CI if a reprint dropped one. Schema and rationale: docs/reprint-survival.md. This ledger was created by the fix for issue #249.

handfixes.summary: the MCP tenant gate falls through to the tool handler when no platform source is registered, instead of default-denying every non-mirror tool
handfixes.why: cli.VerifyMCPInvocation returns (nil, nil) when registeredPlatformSource is nil, which means 'there is nothing to gate' - and no connector in this repo registers a platform source (registerPlatformSource has zero callers outside internal/cli/platform_client.go). The 4.30.1/4.30.2 gate read that nil session as a failure and answered 'MCP tenant gate is not configured' for every tool that is not a Cobra mirror. Cobra mirrors carry pp:tenant-gate = "child-cli" and pass through, so the damage was invisible in a tool count: 6 tools per connector were dead while the server still listed them. Those 6 are the entire offline-mirror surface (context, search, sql) plus the entire code-orchestration surface (<prefix>_search / _get / _execute) - exactly the capabilities this connector's own description says a plain read-only MCP does not ship. Measured over stdio before the fix: 6/6 returned isError with the gate message; after, all 6 reach their handler. Fixed upstream in cli-printing-press 4.30.3 (issue #4157, PR #4171); this is the surgical back-port, byte-identical to what 4.30.3 emits. TestMCPUngatedInvocationUsesRealVerifier is the regression test that ships with the 4.30.3 template: it drives the wrapper with the REAL verifier (not the fake the other two tests install) and fails if the handler is blocked. Reverting either the fall-through or the test fails check_handfixes.py.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Already fixed in the press at 4.30.3 (mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#4171). A reprint on 4.30.3 or later regenerates both the fall-through and the conformance test, so this entry exists to keep the back-port from being dropped by a reprint on an older engine or by a regen-merge that resurrects the 4.30.2 body.

asserts.not_contains: NewToolResultError("MCP tenant gate is not configured")

handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real GET endpoint with the real credential and refuses to dial a placeholder base_url, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and never checking the credential
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every SKILL, guide and docs page tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one. It called any HTTP response to `GET /` "reachable" and rendered it green, so a base_url aimed at the vendor's web UI (where every API path 404s) and a token rejected with 401 on every call both produced an all-green report. On this connector family it also never probed the credential at all: it printed "present, not verified" and left the operator to guess. The mirror defect: a connector whose shipped base_url default is a placeholder dialled the placeholder host, and the DNS failure rendered as "FAIL API: unreachable" - telling a correctly-credentialled operator they were broken without naming the one variable that would fix it. Several placeholder hosts resolve through live wildcard DNS and answer real HTTP, so dialling one produced a confident green verdict against a stranger's server. Measured and gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py. See issue #282. Restated for the press 4.35.1 reprint (2026-11-02): doctorBaseURLIsPlaceholder and doctorIsInfoKey are native to the 4.35.1 doctor.go, so the hand file doctor_verdict.go keeps only the credential probe; the assert follows the function. The shipped doctorShippedBaseURL was Auvik's real US1 regional API root, so doctor told every US1 operator who never set AUVIK_BASE_URL that the install was a placeholder and skipped the credential probe (press-traps section 5). The 4.35.1 native check refuses only templates and RFC 2606 hosts; the test pins both directions.

handfixes.summary: every operator credential this connector reads is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md (manual install)
handfixes.why: Issue #282 ('three live-verified connectors prompt for the wrong credentials'). A connector is installed through THREE independent channels that each carry their own copy of the credential list: manifest.json server.mcp_config.env (what the .mcpb bundle hands Claude Desktop, which has no shell profile, no config.toml and no export - so an undeclared variable is a variable nobody is ever asked for), server.json environmentVariables (the MCP Registry publish channel), and mcp-install.md's copy-paste JSON blocks plus its remote launch line (the manual path, which never touches the bundle at all). The fleet-wide audit found 60 of 65 connectors under-declaring 122 operator-facing variables in the manifest, 61 of 65 mcp-install.md pages omitting 125, and hudu's server.json missing the base URL its manifest marks required. For auvik the manifest gained: AUVIK_TENANT, AUVIK_USER_AGENT, PRINTING_PRESS_CLIENT_PROFILE. server.json gained: AUVIK_TENANT, AUVIK_USER_AGENT, PRINTING_PRESS_CLIENT_PROFILE. mcp-install.md's env blocks gained: AUVIK_TENANT, AUVIK_USER_AGENT, PRINTING_PRESS_CLIENT_PROFILE. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are ALL regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on an UPDATE or re-onboard, so without this ledger a regeneration silently drops every declaration and CI stays green (check_env_schema.py is wired --warn). The asserts below name the specific credentials, not a count, so dropping one and adding another cannot cancel out.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit server.mcp_config.env, the matching user_config prompts, server.json environmentVariables and mcp-install.md's env blocks from ONE declaration of the connector's operator-facing environment, so the three channels cannot be generated out of step. Until then check_env_schema.py compares all three and this ledger pins them.

handfixes.summary: `recall` and `playbook list` are annotated mcp:local-write, not mcp:read-only, because both open the writable learn store and record a row (issue #275 finding 4)
handfixes.why: issue #275 finding 4. `recall` (teach.go) declared mcp:read-only=true, opened the WRITABLE store via store.OpenWithContext and inserted a learn event on every call; `playbook list` (teach_playbook.go) was marked read-only and appended an audit record. The annotation is what an MCP host reads to decide what to auto-approve, so a false one is the same defect class as a doctor command that reports credentials fine without ever checking them: the promise, not the write, is the harm. The replacement is mcp:local-write, a tier this same engine already defines and already uses for `teach` and `playbook amend`: writes land only in the CLI's own local store, never in external state and never in a user-visible file, so the walker registers destructiveHint=false and openWorldHint=false while leaving readOnlyHint unset. Measured at the live MCP server before and after: recall and playbook_list went from readOnlyHint=true, openWorldHint=true to readOnlyHint=false, destructiveHint=false, openWorldHint=false. AGENTS.md is press-generated and carried the same claim in prose, so the annotation sentence there was regenerated from the booted server's tools/list and is pinned by the AGENTS.md asserts below. This is a TRUTH fix, not a behaviour fix - the RunE bodies are untouched and both commands still write exactly what they wrote before. Upstream closed this wontfix (mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#3555), so a reprint reintroduces the false annotation and this ledger is the only thing that catches it.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Upstream declined (mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#3555), so there is nothing to encode in the press today. If that is ever revisited, the rule is mechanical rather than a judgement call: a command whose RunE reaches store.OpenWithContext, appendLearningsAudit or any Insert must not carry mcp:read-only. `learnings list`, `learnings candidates` and `learnings stats` are the remaining teach-loop siblings: each still carries mcp:read-only and each still opens the writable store (creating the database file, running migrations and tightening file modes) though none records a row, and all three were left alone deliberately because the ratified decision named only `recall` and `playbook list`. The same shape is not confined to the teach loop: every command that reads this connector's local mirror opens it through the same read-write call, `analytics` included, so what the press should encode is the mechanical rule above rather than a per-command list.

asserts.contains: // playbook list opens the WRITABLE learn store and appends an
which is narrower than it sounds

handfixes.summary: Every novel command reads its store rows through one family table (auvik_local.go): the CURRENT sync partition first, legacy partition names after, and only rows whose JSON:API type Auvik documents for that family, one row per id (newest synced wins). Every freshness hint and every `sync --resources` instruction names the current partition. Rows an older print left under a partition this build writes another family to move into the current partition (typed, current copy wins) at every writable store open, so the current partition's reconcile governs them.
handfixes.why: Press 4.35.1 renamed Auvik's sync partitions: "inventory" moved from devices to COMPONENTS, "asm" from apps to ASM CLIENTS, "auvik-inventory" from v2 devices to v2 DISCOVERY STATUS. The ported novels read {"inventory","inventory-device-info"} as devices, so eol, inventory diff, configuration audit, usage reconcile and alert noise counted every component as a device; device discovery-gaps read a partition that no longer exists and reported no gaps; asm shadow mixed clients into apps; and every sync instruction told the operator to sync components. auvik_partition_test.go seeds a store in the 4.35.1 shape plus rows an older print left behind and fails on the pre-fix code (seen failing: seen/partition-tests-failing.log); TestAuvikFamiliesPinTheirEndpoint fails the build when a later reprint renames a partition again. Partition authority (review round 2): the earlier fix stopped reading legacy partitions once sync_state showed a completed walk of the current one, but a FILTERED full sync also completes a walk, so legacy d2 vanished after `sync --resources inventory-device-info --full --param filter[deviceType]=switch` returned only d1. The one-time typed move (store/extras.go moveLegacyPartitions, fed by auvikLegacyMoves) hands legacy rows to the current partition before sync walks it; the press reconcile then prunes on an unfiltered full sync and refuses on a filtered one. Both directions are driven through the real sync command (auvik_partition_migration_test.go, seen failing first).
handfixes.spec-encode: The press picks a group's canonical partition by endpoint-name order, so the name moves when the spec's endpoint set changes. x-pp-resource cannot pin it (it flattens the command tree). Ask upstream for an x-pp-sync-name extension; until then the family table plus its endpoint pin is the guard.

handfixes.summary: The root --select help text says what paths select against: API responses have the JSON:API envelope stripped (--select attributes.deviceName), local-store reports are envelopes (--select rows.client).
handfixes.why: The generated example (--select alertDefinitionId,description,detectedOn) names top-level fields that do not exist in either shape this CLI emits, so following the help returned empty objects. Carried from the shipped tree; root.go is generated, so tools/apply_edits.py in the reprint run re-applies it.

handfixes.summary: The MCP context tool lists each novel command's full research.json rationale, not the ~96-character cut press 4.35.1 renders, and carries no unverifiable competitor claim.
handfixes.why: 4.35.1 truncates each novel rationale mid-sentence in internal/mcp/tools.go ("... credentials and device inventory; discoveryStatus has no v1 equivalent"), and the prior research text claimed "no competitor implementation" and "the leading competitor MCP omits all of ASM", which nothing in this repo verifies. research.json now carries the shipped tree's wording; apply_edits.py restores the full text by novel name. Review r1 (2026-11-02) corrected three rationales at the source because they were false: discoveryStatus DOES have a v1 equivalent (deviceDetailsAttributes.discoveryStatus), the usage endpoint DOES list billed devices, and ASM licenses are read per application. The same text also renders as each novel's context "insight", which apply_edits.py now restores too.

handfixes.summary: cliArgsFromMCP refuses, at forward time and whatever blocked set its caller passed, every name in mcpPathFlagFloor (blockedDestinationFlags + blockedInputFlags + from-csv, home, reconcile); UnblockedFilesystemPathFlags fails the build when a regenerated shell-out command grows a local-path flag.
handfixes.why: Press 4.35.1 moved the destination check out of cliArgsFromMCP into the per-command blocked set, so the forward-time floor the shipped tree had (mcp-filesystem-destination-gate) was gone: cliArgsFromMCP({"db": "/tmp/x"}, {}) forwarded --db=/tmp/x (TestMCPCannotDirectTheLocalStore failed on the fresh render). Runtime calls still pass the native blocked set; this keeps the shipped defense in depth and the shipped floor names (never weaker than the published surface). shellout.go is generated: tools/apply_edits.py re-applies the one-line call.

handfixes.summary: go.mod keeps golang.org/x/text at or above the fleet floor v0.42.0; the 4.35.1 render pins v0.14.0.
handfixes.why: GO-2026-5970 (fixed v0.39.0) and GO-2026-6629 (fixed v0.41.0); the fleet floor is v0.42.0 (tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json floors). A reprint that takes the render's pin downgrades it silently while every build stays green.

handfixes.summary: README.md, mcp-install.md and page.json say the ChatGPT desktop app runs this connector locally (STDIO) and that ChatGPT on the web, Microsoft 365 Copilot / Copilot Studio and the Gemini app are not supported by msp-skills yet, with a link to the hosted-gateway comparison; no paid-plan list, no Developer Mode recipe, no 'ChatGPT connects only to remote servers'.
handfixes.why: Docs fix approved 2026-11-03, following PR #502. OpenAI's MCP docs (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/extend/mcp) say the ChatGPT desktop app, Codex CLI and the IDE extension support MCP servers, add them as STDIO, and share MCP configuration; ChatGPT on the web uses remote MCP through plugins and does not read local Codex config. The old text listed ChatGPT plans, said ChatGPT connects only to remote servers, and on the reprinted connectors told users to host the connector over HTTPS for a Developer Mode connector and Copilot Studio; SECURITY.md pauses HTTP mode until each connector is reprinted. README.md, mcp-install.md and page.json are regenerated by msp-skills-publish onboard.py, whose template still writes the old ChatGPT text, so without this entry a re-onboard or reprint silently restores it.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Change the ChatGPT, Microsoft 365 Copilot and Gemini app text in onboard.py (cc-skills msp-skills-publish) so a regeneration writes this wording itself, then this entry can be retired.

asserts.contains: **Not supported by msp-skills yet.** ChatGPT on the web

### Does this work with ChatGPT?

Yes, in the **ChatGPT desktop app**.

asserts.not_contains: Microsoft 365 Copilot, Gemini, and any agent

handfixes.why: Credential leak contract (docs/credential-leak-contract.md), owner GO 2026-10-29: one implementation, wired by hand, checked by credkit_verify. A reprint regenerates every template file this entry asserts on and would drop the routing silently; the leak tests in internal/credwire/leak_test.go drive the built binaries for each credential class (token echo, origin, journal, startup output, startup credential, --stdin body), each seen failing on the pre-kit build.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: generate the kit wiring, the Declarations literal and one kit-wrapped SQLite driver name.

handfixes.summary: sync walks every Auvik list page by page: page[first] as the page size, the page[after] cursor taken from links.next, and no page[last] on the request. Without it every sync stopped at page one, reported sync_complete, and a --full sync pruned every mirrored row past the first 100.
handfixes.spec-encode: The press emits empty determinePaginationDefaults and resourceSupportsPagination switches for this spec because Auvik's JSON:API paging (page[first]/page[after] with links.next) is not a pagination shape the profiler detects. Ask upstream to detect page[first]+page[after] as a cursor paginator; until then this hand-fix is the guard.
handfixes.why: Codex round 1 of the 4.35.1 reprint review; executed against the built binary with a two-page fake (.review/probe-sync): before the fix one request, total 2, the page-two device absent from search; after it two requests and all three devices stored. The same empty switches ship on main's 4.30.2 build.

handfixes.summary: sync wraps the event writer its parallel workers share in syncSerialWriter (internal/cli/sync_event_writer.go), so two workers never call Write on it at once.
handfixes.why: The generated sync hands cmd.OutOrStdout() (or ErrOrStderr() in machine output) to every --concurrency worker, and each writes sync_start, progress and error events. os.Stdout tolerates that; the writers --deliver (a mirror into a bytes.Buffer) and --receipt-file / --audit-dir (a running SHA-256) install do not, nor does an in-process caller's buffer: Windows CI on PR #655 panicked in bytes.Buffer.grow from syncResource, and go test -race found 28 races on veeam. TestSyncWorkerPoolSerializesEventWrites pins it. A reprint regenerates sync.go and drops the wrap; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-event-writer-serialized).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side (mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#5369): the sync template should serialize the event writer its top-level worker pool shares, as its dependent path already does with lockedWriter.

handfixes.summary: the adaptive limiter's blind ramp raises only a rate the last Wait slept on, so sync's rate_rps reports a real pace
handfixes.why: On a header-less API the ramp multiplied the rate by 1.25 every 10 successes with no ceiling: mcp2's hubspot sync printed rate_rps 6.6e24 (about 2,500 requests), and after such a ramp a 429's halving could no longer slow a single request. A rate the requests never reach is no longer raised. Re-applied after a reprint by replay_handfixes.py (recipe limiter-paced).

handfixes.summary: a resource the vendor refuses this token (HTTP 403) is recorded as skipped and no longer holds store_status at partial; a resource that errored stays partial and is named.
handfixes.why: A 403 resource never completes, so its sync_state row stayed at 0 and store_status read partial for good after a clean exit 0 (#692). store_status now says complete_with_skips only when every other resource finished, and search, sql and sync_summary name what was skipped or failed. A reprint regenerates sync.go and mcp/tools.go and drops this; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-forbidden-not-partial).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: sync should record a resource the vendor refuses separately from one that failed (not filed yet).

handfixes.summary: sync_progress reports measured rows per second (rows_per_sec, and rate_rps as the same value); the limiter's ceiling is limiter_ceiling_rps.
handfixes.why: The generated sync printed the adaptive limiter's ceiling as rate_rps and as req/s on the human line, so 4.9 was reported while the sync stored 33 rows a second (#694). A reprint regenerates sync.go and brings it back; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-progress-measured-rate).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the sync template should report a measured rate and name the limiter's ceiling separately (not filed yet).

handfixes.summary: sync writes at most one sync_progress line per resource every 5 seconds (the first page always reports; sync_complete carries the final count), instead of one per page.
handfixes.why: Every write to stdout or stderr costs a full credential check whatever its size, and sync wrote one progress line per page: 74% of hubspot sync's CPU at a real server's pace (#696). A reprint regenerates sync.go with one line per page; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies the guard (fleet_handfixes.json sync-progress-throttled).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the sync template's per-page progress line should be throttled, as its dependent walk already is (not filed yet).

handfixes.summary: The <api>_search tool's description ends with the API's resource families (codeOrchSearchResources in internal/mcp/search_desc.go, from codeOrchEndpoints, capped at 300 characters).
handfixes.why: The generated description was the same in every connector and named no resource, so a host that ranks tools by words put other tools above <api>_search for "<api> <resource>" (#629; zammad_search ranked 13th of 45 for "zammad tickets"). A reprint regenerates code_orch.go without the call; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json mcp-search-desc-resources).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side (upstream PR named in fleet_handfixes.json): the code-orchestration template should build the <api>_search description from the endpoint registry's resource families.
